texts.preamble: Rekha N vs Murugesh on 7 April, 2022 Kabc020137942020 Before The Court Of Xxiv Additional Small Causes Judge And The Motor Accident Claims Tribunal & A.C.M.M. (Scch26) At Bengaluru Dated This The 7th April 2022 Present: Sri.R.Mahesha. B.A.L.Llb., Xxiv Addl. Scj & Acmm & Member Mact Bengaluru. M.V.C No.3028/2020
texts.facts: : The petition is filed by the Petitioner under Sec.166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1989 seeking compensation for an amount of Rs.8,50,000/ for the grievous injuries sustained by her, in road traffic accident. 2. The brief facts of the case of the Petitioner is as follows: That on 2772020 at about 10.30 a.m. when the petitioner was riding moped bearing reg.No.KA04JW8362 slowly, carefully and cautiously by following traffic rules on left side of the road on Mathikere main road, Mathikere bus stop, Bangalore city, Bangalore, at that time, driver of the auto bearing reg.no.KA02AB0477 came with high speed and in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against petitioner's moped, as a result of which petitioner sustained fracture of lateral condyle of left tibia, abrasion over the right anterior aspect of the leg and other injuries all over the body. That immediately petitioner was shifted to Sumathi hospital, Bangalore wherein she took first aid treatment, thereafter she was shifted to V.P.Magnus hospital, Nelamangala wherein she was admitted as inpatient for 25 days and surgery was done and incurred Rs.1,50,000/ towards medicine, treatment, conveyance, attendant charges etc., Due to accidental injuries petitioner is suffering from permanent disability. That prior to the accident, petitioner was hale and healthy and was working as tailor and earning Rs.25,000/p.m. and due to accidental injuries she lost her income. Hence petitioner prays to award compensation of Rs.8,50,000/ from the respondents. 3. After service of summons, the respondent No.1RC owner of the auto remained exparte and respondent No.2 insurer of the offending vehicle has appeared through its counsel and filed its written statement. 4. Respondent No.2 in written statement stated that this respondent has issued a liability only policy for commercial vehicle policy bearing No.OG2017011831 00004263 In favour of first respondent in respect of autorickshaw bearing No.KA02AB477 and it is valid from 15102019 to 14102020 and their liability, if any is strictly in terms and conditions, exceptions, limits and endorsement of the policy and subject to compliance of 64VB of insurance Act and law governing thereto. That the first respondent had violated the mandatory provisions i.e., Section 134(c) and section 158(6) of MV Act 1989. That the owner/insured and jurisdictional police ought to have intimated about the alleged accident to the insurer of the motor vehicle which involved in the Rekha N vs Murugesh on 7 April, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/133837927/ 2 accident as required under the aforesaid provisions. That they have failed to comply with the section 134(c) and 158(6) of MV Act. That after lapse of one day, the petitioner has filed a false case against insured vehicle to cause wrongful loss to this respondent. That it is clear breach of terms and conditions of policy and also violation of section 149(2) of MV Act 1988. That accident had occurred due to rash and negligent riding the motor cycle by the petitioner herself who did not have DL and not wearing the safety helmet. Hence prays to dismiss the petition. 5. 6. In order to prove the above said issues, Petitioner has been examined as PW1 and got marked Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.20 documents. One Dr.Manjunath Biradar got examined as PW2 and got marked ExP21 to 24. One Dr.Nagaraj B.N. got examined as PW3 and got marked Ex P25 and 26. 8. In order to prove the actionable negligence, the petitioner herself entered into the witness box and filed her affidavit in lieu of examinationinchief and got examined as P.W.1 and got marked ExP1 to 19. PW1 reiterates the averments and the allegations made in the claim petition and Rekha N vs Murugesh on 7 April, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/133837927/ 3 deposed that, the accident has occurred solely due to the negligent driving of the auto bearing reg.No.KA02AB0477. 11. The informant stated in complaint/FIS that on 2772020 at about 10.30 a.m., when she was going on her scooter bearing KA04JW8362, BEL circle to HMT main road, at Mattikere bus stop driver of the autorickshaw bearing No.KA02AB0477 came with high speed and negligent manner and dashed against her, as a result of which she fell down and sustained injuries to her left leg and scooter also damaged, thereafter public were shifted her from the said auto to Sumathi hospital wherein xray was done and informed doctor was not available, then for better treatment, she was admitted as inpatient at V.P.Magnus hospital, Nelamangala. Therefore petitioner lodged complaint on 2872020. Accordingly the SHO of Yashwanthpur traffic police recorded FIR and proceed to conduct investigation. The investigation officer proceeded to spot and conduct spot panchanama and filed charge sheet against driver of the autorickshaw bearing No.KA 02AB 0477 for the offence punishable u/s 337, 338 of IPC Section 134(B) r/w section 187 IMV Act. 13.
texts.arguments: The main defence of the respondent No.2 is that he denied entire case of petitioner and specifically contended that there is a delay of one day in lodging complaint, the petitioner has not having DL. That first respondent had been willfully entrusted his vehicle to a person who did not possess valid and effective DL to drive the same as on the date of accident. That first respondent allowed to ply his vehicle on the road without possessing valid permit and fitness certificate as on the date of accident. 14. In addenda of this, in a claim for compensation U/S.166 of MV Act, 1988, the claimant is to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and the standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by Hon'ble Apex Court in the decision reported in 2011 SAR (Civil) 319 (Kusum and others Vs. Satbir and others). As per the recent decision of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in the case between MFA 4893/2016(MV) Smt.Yashodamma Vs M.D., BMTC disposed on 1610 2020 (DB) held that in case no document produced by the petitioners to prove their avocation and income, in such a situation, court can refer or rely the guidelines issued by Karnataka State Legal Service Authority to assess notional income of injured. Therefore Notional Income of Rs.14,500/ p.m. The petitioner states that in the said accident, she sustained fracture lateral condyle of left tibia, partial thickness tear ACL with avulsion fracture tibial intercondylor eminence, comminuted mildly displaced fracture tibia and fibula, avulsion injury patellar tendon and other injuries to all over the body. That the petitioner underwent surgery. That the petitioner now complains of unable to sit down, squat and sit cross leg, unable to pedal the tailoring machine and carry her profession as tailor. So far as the compensation under non pecuniary damages, considering the fact that the petitioner has suffered permanent disability to the extent of 5% due to the accident which cause to her immeasurable mental agony and pain, I am opinion that an amount of Rs.10,000/ would be just and fair compensation under the head of pain and sufferings. 18. Loss of Amenities of Life : The petitioner had sustained fracture lateral condyle of left tibia, partial thickness tear ACL with avulsion fracture tibial intercondylor eminence, comminuted mildly displaced fracture tibia and fibula, avulsion injury patellar tendon and other injuries to all over the body. For loss of amenities of life, undoubtedly she has to lead her life ahead and she is sure to suffer on her day today activities. Hence petitioner is awarded Rs.10,000/ under loss of amenities of life. 19. Medical Expenses: The petitioner has stated that she spent Rs.1,50,000/ towards medicine, treatment. The petitioner has produced ExP9medical bills (19) Rs.1,09,826/, ExP10advance receipts (2), ExP11medical prescriptions (3). From the medical records produced by the petitioner, it discloses that petitioner took treatment at V.P.Magnus hospital, Nelamangala as inpatient from 2772020 to 3072020 and underwent surgery. On perusal of ExP9, it indicates that the petitioner paid Rs.82,600/. The hospital authorities gave discount of Rs.350/. But petitioner claimed Rs.82,950/. 24. As far as awarding of interest on the compensation amount is concerned, in a recent decision reported in 2018 ACJ 1300 between Mangla Ram V/s. Oriental Insurance Co., Ltd., and others (in CA Nos.2499 of 2018 arising out of SLP(C) Nos.2814142 of 2017 decided on 06.04.2018) wherein the Hon'ble Supreme Court with regard to interest at the rate of 9% p.a. on the compensation amount, in para No.28 of the judgment held that, 'The appellant would also be entitled to interest on the total amount of compensation at the rate of 9 per cent per annum on the compensation from the date of filing of the claim petition till date of realization" and also by following the principles laid down in (2018) ACJ 1020 in between ICICI Lombard General Insurance Co., Ltd., V/s. Ajay Kumar Mohanty and another decided on 6.3.2018 (in CA Nos.7181 of 2015 and 1879 of 2016) at para No.1 and 12 Hon'ble Supreme Court held that: "Quantum InterestTribunal allowed interest at the rate of 7.5 per cent which was reduced by High Court to 7 per centApex Court allowed interest at 9 per cent per annum from the date of filing of claim application".
